android.desc:
The Original Classic Endless Running Adventure!
Experience the thrill and challenge of Temple Run – the classic global endless runner game that redefined mobile gaming!
Steal the cursed idol and escape from the relentless Demon Monkeys in a heart-pounding adventure through ancient temples, jungle ruins, and precarious cliff edges.
Outrun danger in the ultimate maze-running, jungle-escaping, temple adventure!
- Run through the jungle as you swipe to turn, jump, dash, parkour, and slide past deadly obstacles and traps
- Race through temples, bridges, and treacherous paths
- Collect coins, unlock diverse heroes, and boost your power-ups to reach super sonic speeds through the jungle 
- Test your reflexes in a fast and frenzied arcade action experience
- Challenge friends & climb the leaderboards online 
- No WiFi game, no internet needed: Enjoy endless fun offline without an internet connection. Temple Run is perfect game to play on the go. 

Accolades: 
Temple Run is that heart-pounding action movie moment – but non-stop! – SlideToPlay
One of the most thrilling and fun running games ever! – TheAppera
A fast and frenzied experience. – IGN
Very addicting… a truly different running game! – Appolicious

Join over 500 MILLION players worldwide in this legendary treasure hunting running game and escape the jungle with the idol!

Download now and challenge yourself to see how far you can run from the demon monkey!

quotes.text:
This article is overblown.

In Android you don't have to support any device you don't want to, just exclude it from being shown to those users. Same with the OS version, if you don't want to support 1.6 you can make it unavailable to those users.

Most apps don't have fragmentation problems unless you're doing something tricky and hardware dependent, like trying to do fancy things with the camera. I've released several semi-popular apps with few bug complaints.

If you look at Temple Run in Play you will see it is very highly rated and it has over a million downloads. https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.imangi.templerun

Finally, the author's link to one badly voted Reddit comment with little discussion made me think he was just out to write an Android bashing article as link bait.
quotes.story_title: The shocking toll of hardware and software fragmentation on Android development
